newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-ESCO MUST SIGN SHIPPING DEAL BY JULY 10.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-ESCO MUST SIGN SHIPPING DEAL BY JULY 10.

text.p: ESCO Holdings, chosen to buy a 70 percent stake in the Estonian Shipping Company, must sign a privatisation agreement by July 10 at the latest, the privatisation agency said on Wednesday.
"If ESCO does not sign the agreement under its offered conditions by July 10, the agreement will be signed with Arbonale," Transport Minister Raivo Vare told a news conference.
"The board of the privatisation agency evaluated the business plans and forecasts for the future...the decision was taken based on overwhelming majority," Vare added.
ESCO is held 50 percent by Norwegian Tschudi & Eitzen, 12 percent by Uhisinvesteeringud, the investment arm Uhispank and 10 percent by U.S. Stanton Capital.

Rival bidder Arbonale was formed by Talinvest and Hansa Investments, Estonian oil fuel terminal N-Terminaal, Norwegian shipper Navigator, investment bank Nomura and Hong Kong shipper Jinhui Shipping and Transportation Ltd .
Vare said the deadline gave the second bidder an opportunity to sign the deal and pushed the winner to act quickly.
Vare said the sale of Estonian Shipping was one of the biggest privatisation deals in Estonia and the first deal with big infrastructure companies.
